title: From HAL to Her: AI Philosophy Through the Lens of Pop Culture
affiliations: University of Maine

detail.title: From HAL to Her: AI Philosophy Through the Lens of Pop Culture
detail.abstract: This paper examines how AI is represented in literature, film, and TV, and the ethical insights these portrayals offer when viewed through the lens of computer ethics and the philosophy of technology. Through a thematic analysis of selected cultural works, it identifies recurring motifs - such as autonomy, emotional intelligence, techno-authoritarianism, and surveillance - and considers their relevance to contemporary socio-political debates on AI. The paper critiques dominant real-world narratives of hype, competition, and dystopian catastrophe (e.g., the Terminator/Frankenstein trope), arguing that they obscure more grounded and socially responsible understandings of technological change. Instead, it advances a framework of technological realism, positioned between optimism, pessimism, determinism, and somnambulism, as a more constructive stance. Bridging popular culture and applied ethics, this interdisciplinary study contributes to a more context-sensitive and critically reflective discourse on AI. The paper concludes by highlighting directions for future research, including the underexplored role of video games in shaping AI imaginaries.

title: Co-Evolutionary Synergies Between Generative AI and Digital Transformation: A Dynamic Capabilities-Resource-Based Framework for Innovation and Resilience

detail.abstract: This conceptual study examines how Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) and Digital Transformation (DT) jointly function as strategic enablers of Business Model Innovation (BMI) and Organizational Resilience (OR). Despite the rapid expansion of AI-enabled transformation, theoretical clarity remains limited regarding the mechanisms through which cognitive (GenAI) and structural (DT) digital capabilities co-evolve to enhance strategic renewal. Drawing on the Resource-Based View (RBV) and Dynamic Capabilities View (DCV), the paper develops an integrated framework that positions GenAI and DT simultaneously as VRIN digital resources and as sensing-seizing dynamic capabilities. The proposed model theorizes a synergistic capability system in which GenAI and DT enable continuous BMI, which subsequently strengthens OR as a meta-capability that reinforces adaptive learning and reconfiguration. Five theoretical propositions articulate the pathways linking digital complementarity to innovation and resilience. The study contributes to strategic management and digital transformation scholarship by offering a unified DCV-RBV lens that explains how AI-enabled organizations build recursive, self-reinforcing cycles of sensing, innovation, and resilience. Practical and policy implications highlight the importance of designing integrated AI-DT ecosystems that support sustainable competitiveness in volatile environments.

title: The Economics of Algorithmic Personalization: Evidence from an Educational Technology Platform
affiliations: Stanford University, Stanford Graduate School of Business, Stanford University, University of Georgia and Northeastern University

detail.title: The Economics of Algorithmic Personalization: Evidence from an Educational Technology Platform
detail.abstract: Can personalized recommendations improve engagement in educational technology? We design, test, and scale a collaborative filtering system for Freadom, an English-learning app for Indian children. A randomized controlled trial (RCT) shows that personalization, deployed in a single content section, increases engagement by 60% in that section and by 14% app-wide. We then exploit an eligibility threshold in a regression discontinuity design (RDD) to track effects over five months of deployment. For user cohorts receiving personalization during deployment, RDD estimates exceed RCT benchmark by a factor of 2.5, opposite of the "voltage drop" typically observed in policy scale-ups. This provides evidence that, for algorithmic interventions, RCT estimates may be lower bounds on scaled impact rather than upper bounds. However, personalization benefits are front-loaded. Gains concentrate in users' first weeks, with diminishing returns thereafter. This pattern, combined with the sharp decline in predicted match quality as users exhaust their best content matches, suggests that content availability rather than algorithmic sophistication becomes the binding constraint.

detail.title: Design and Development of a Multi-Role B2B ECommerce Platform for Business Management
detail.abstract: In today's digital era, large e-commerce platforms have transformed global trade, yet small and medium local retailers still struggle to adapt to digital systems. Our Project is a JavaFX-based B2B e-commerce application designed to empower local business owners, shopkeepers, and delivery partners through one integrated platform. It enables easy product addition, order management, and delivery coordination using a modular structure and cloud database. The system uses Google Firestore for real-time data storage and retrieval and JavaFX for a modern, interactive user interface. The main objective is to bridge the gap between traditional businesses and digital commerce by providing a reliable, scalable, and easy-to-use desktop application. Testing and user feedback show significant improvement in operational efficiency, real-time synchronization, and overall user satisfaction.

detail.abstract: This review systematically investigates the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Business Intelligence (BI) to enhance operational efficiency in the manufacturing sector. The analysis highlights AI's transformative role in reshaping strategic decision-making, operational processes, and value creation mechanisms across manufacturing industries. Key thematic areas include the deployment of AI for improved manufacturing performance, the evolution of smart manufacturing systems, the integration of BI frameworks within AI applications, and the implementation of predictive and prescriptive analytics. Additionally, the review explores the intersection of AI with emerging technologies such as machine learning and next-generation analytics in areas including process optimization, quality control, and organizational capability development. Responsible and ethical AI adoption identified as not only a moral obligation but also a strategic imperative that enhances competitiveness and operational agility. This review provides practical, evidence-based frameworks for practitioners to align AI capabilities with organizational objectives and identifies key avenues for future research, including longitudinal assessments, context-specific implementation strategies, and sustainable innovation pathways. The findings position AI as a driver of systemic transformation in manufacturing, necessitating continuous learning, ethical governance, and strategic foresight to sustain competitive advantage in increasingly digitized industrial environments.

detail.abstract:
Digital Financial Literacy (DFL) is pivotal for financial inclusion and sustainable development in the Pacific Islands, yet significant disparities persist across nations. This brief introduces a four-dimensional DFL Index and applies machine learning-based clustering to analyze readiness across seven countries: Fiji, Papua New Guinea, Solomon Islands, Timor-Leste, Vanuatu, Samoa, and Tonga. Findings reveal that digital skills and trust, not adoption alone, drive positive financial outcomes, with Fiji leading in readiness and other nations lagging due to infrastructure and competency gaps.

The analysis identifies three distinct clusters and highlights critical factors influencing DFL, including gender equity, cybersecurity awareness, and localized education. Based on these insights, the brief proposes evidence-based policy recommendations:

1.      Expand rural connectivity and affordable internet access;

2.     Deliver targeted digital financial training for women and youth;

3.     Build trust through cybersecurity literacy and consumer protection;

4.     Foster public–private partnerships for scalable, localized programs.

By addressing these priorities, policymakers can bridge regional divides, enhance resilience, and unlock economic potential in the digital era. This brief offers a strategic roadmap for inclusive digital transformation, grounded in robust data analytics and regional collaboration.

detail.abstract:
This annex defines the measurement, governance, and evidentiary requirements for managing External AI Representation Risk. This risk arises when AI-generated claims about an enterprise, its products, services, or practices are unstable, unsupported, misattributed, or misleading, and are subsequently relied upon in enterprise decision-making. This annex governs:

• identification and classification of AI-generated claims,
• measurement of claim stability and drift,
• control of claim inclusion in decision-exposed outputs,
• production of audit-grade evidence to support governance decisions.

This annex does not govern or constrain the behavior of external AI systems. It governs enterprise reliance, propagation, escalation, and evidentiary treatment of AI outputs. 2. Core Governance Principle Enterprise risk arises not from whether an AI statement is true, but from whether an unstable, unsupported, or misattributed claim is relied upon as if it were stable, evidentiary, or authoritative.

detail.abstract:
The WannaCry ransomware attack of 2017 disrupted health systems, transportation sectors, telecommunications, and public services across more than 150 countries. As a result, governments and private organizations recognized the importance of technology innovation management, secure infrastructure, and policies that reinforce societal resilience.

This paper evaluates the role of frameworks that support technology innovation and security management within critical societal infrastructure. It assesses theoretical and conceptual frameworks, examines how they integrate with infrastructure environments, and recommends one primary and one supporting framework for analyzing and mitigating technology risks. It applies industry-standard models—including the NIST Cybersecurity Framework (NIST CSF) and Enterprise Architecture (EA)—to evaluate the strengths and weaknesses of existing IT policies in the context of the WannaCry incident.

title: Dual Privacy Protection in Financial AI: When k-Anonymity and Differential Privacy Improve Accuracy Together

detail.title: Dual Privacy Protection in Financial AI: When k-Anonymity and Differential Privacy Improve Accuracy Together
detail.abstract: Privacy-preserving machine learning typically trades accuracy for privacy guarantees. We challenge this assumption by demonstrating dual privacy protection that simultaneously improves model performance. Our system combines kanonymity (k≥5) for structural re-identification prevention with (ε, δ)-differential privacy for statistical inference protection. Through experiments on enterprise credit risk prediction across three financial institutions, we reveal: (1) k-anonymity preprocessing achieves 98.7% anonymization quality while maintaining accuracy (93.09% → 93.12%), (2) DP-SGD increases test accuracy from 93.09% to 95.66% (+2.57%), demonstrating DP's implicit regularization effect, and (3) combining k-anonymity, DP, and federated learning yields 98.28% accuracy (+5.19% total improvement). Our dual-layer approach addresses complementary attack vectors: k-anonymity prevents attribute-combination attacks (e.g., identifying companies via industry+region+size), while differential privacy prevents statistical inference attacks (e.g., deducing individual records from aggregates). The 6× reduction in training-validation gap (0.06 → 0.01) and 27% lower weight norm confirm DP's regularization benefit. This establishes a new paradigm where rigorous privacy protection enhances rather than hinders model performance, with immediate implications for regulated industries requiring both structural and mathematical privacy guarantees.

title: Persistence of Gender Norms and Women Entrepreneurship
affiliations: University of Zurich and Copenhagen Business School

detail.title: Persistence of Gender Norms and Women Entrepreneurship

publicationDetails.journalName: IZA Institute of Labor Economics Discussion Paper Series

detail.abstract: We study whether gender norms—proxied by Switzerland’s 1981 referendum on constitutional gender equality—continue to shape women’s entrepreneurship today, despite major demographic change. Using startup data for all Swiss municipalities from 2016 to 2023, we find that places with stronger historical support for gender equality have significantly higher women-to-men startup ratios. A one–percentage point increase in the 1981 “yes” vote share is associated with a 0.165 percent increase in this ratio. The result is robust to controlling for later gender-related referenda, extensive municipal characteristics, and contemporary policy measures. The association is stronger in municipalities with more stable populations and in less religious municipalities. Childcare spending alone is not linked to startup rates, but it positively affects women’s entrepreneurship when combined with supportive historical gender norms, highlighting the joint role of formal policies and informal social support.

title: AI Tutoring Enhances Student Learning Without Crowding Out Reading Effort
affiliations: WZB Berlin Social Science Center, University of Göttingen and WHU - Otto Beisheim School of Management

detail.title: AI Tutoring Enhances Student Learning Without Crowding Out Reading Effort

publicationDetails.journalName: IZA Institute of Labor Economics Discussion Paper Series

detail.abstract: We study how AI tutoring affects learning in higher education through a randomized experiment with 334 university students preparing for an incentivized exam. Students either received only textbook material, restricted access to an AI tutor requiring initial independent reading, or unrestricted access throughout the study period. AI tutor access raises test performance by 0.23 standard deviations relative to control. Surprisingly, unrestricted access significantly outperforms restricted access by 0.21 standard deviations, contradicting concerns about premature AI reliance. Behavioral analysis reveals that unrestricted access fosters gradual integration of AI support, while restricted access induces intensive bursts of prompting that disrupt learning flow. Benefits are heterogeneous: AI tutors prove most effective for students with lower baseline knowledge and stronger self-regulation skills, suggesting that seamless AI integration enhances learning when students can strategically combine independent study with targeted support.

title: The impact of wildfire smoke on local avian biodiversity
affiliations: University of Exeter and University of Bern

detail.title: The impact of wildfire smoke on local avian biodiversity
detail.abstract: Land use alternations and climate change are shifting natural fire regimes, leading to prolonged and intensified fire seasons accompanied by widespread air pollution, with potentially important consequences for local wildlife. Combining data from the North American Breeding Bird Survey with high-resolution satellite imagery, we estimate the impact of wildfire-specific smoke pollution (PM2.5) on avian biodiversity in the contiguous United States (US) from 2008 to 2022. The panel fixed effects instrumental variable estimation results indicate a short-term adverse effect of PM2.5 on taxonomic and phylogenetic diversity metrics. More specifically, a standard deviation (sd) increase in wildfire-specific PM2.5 pollution reduces species richness, abundance, and phylogenetic diversity by about 0.1 sd, largely driven by observations in the Western US. For the most polluted transects the effect is up to 2-3 standard deviations. The adverse effects on biodiversity metrics vary markedly across ecosystems. While the decrease in phylogenetic diversity is most pronounced in the Western US, for the taxonomic metrics it is the Eastern Temperate Forests, the Northern Forests, and the North American Deserts, which are driving the adverse effect of wildfire smoke. These findings underscore the need for targeted fire management and conservation strategies to mitigate biodiversity loss, especially in the face of increasing wildfire intensity and smoke exposure projected for many regions worldwide.

title: Filling the Void: How Competing Brands Can Capitalize on a Brand Deletion
affiliations: University of North Carolina (UNC) at Chapel Hill - Marketing Area and University of New South Wales

detail.title: Filling the Void: How Competing Brands Can Capitalize on a Brand Deletion

publicationDetails.detailsText: Kilts Center at Chicago Booth Marketing Data Center Paper
publicationDetails.journalName: Kilts Center at Chicago Booth Marketing Data Center Paper Series

detail.abstract: Brand manufacturers, big and small, regularly prune their brand portfolios by deleting their brands from categories. Competing brands try to fill the void, with potentially varying consequences for sister brands by the same manufacturer, rival national brands, and private labels. As little is known about these consequences, this research analyzes systematically whether these three brand types benefit and how they adjust their marketing conduct following a brand deletion. Using a difference-in-differences analysis of 1,046 FMCG national brand deletions observed over 10 years affecting competing brands sold across 201 US markets and 55 retailers (with about 63,000 market-retailer-category-brand combinations affected), the findings reveal that the outcomes of the deletions are strongly shaped by how brands adjust their marketing mix after the brand deletion. By lifting distribution (which is highly effective), private labels are the largest beneficiaries of brand deletions, followed by sister brands (successfully lifting line length), and, lastly, rival national brands. There are also lost opportunities (little change in price promotion across brand types, spoiled arms (hike in ineffective feature advertising), and self-inflicted losses (regular price hikes that decrease revenue). Manufacturers retain only 38% of the deleted brand’s revenue through sister brands on average, showing the risk of brand pruning.

title: Immigration and Education: Early Insights from the Buslift to New York City
affiliations: City University of New York (CUNY) - CUNY Graduate Center and University of California, Riverside

detail.title: Immigration and Education: Early Insights from the Buslift to New York City

publicationDetails.journalName: IZA Institute of Labor Economics Discussion Paper Series

detail.abstract: Since 2022, New York City has received more than 200,000 asylum-seekers from the southern border, many of whom were young children. Families were placed in homeless shelters, with children subsequently enrolled in nearby public elementary schools. Exploiting variation in homeless shelter capacity across school zones, we show that exposed schools saw increases in migrant students, proxied by English Language Learners, Hispanic students, and students in temporary housing. Despite these shifts, domestic students did not experience adverse impacts on enrollment, test scores, attendance, or chronic absenteeism. Progressive funding helped buffer schools against resource crowding, expanding English language instruction to accommodate newcomers.

title: The Psychology of Consumer Choices: How Emotional Triggers Influence Teen Spending Behaviour in Digital Markets
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: The Psychology of Consumer Choices: How Emotional Triggers Influence Teen Spending Behaviour in Digital Markets
detail.abstract: This research paper explores how emotional triggers shape the consumer behaviour of teenagers in digital markets. With the rapid expansion of social media and e-commerce platforms, online environments have become powerful spaces where emotions often outweigh logic in purchasing decisions. Drawing from consumer psychology and behavioural economics, the study investigates how factors such as social validation, fear of missing out (FOMO), instant gratification, and identity formation influence teen spending behaviour. It further examines how digital marketing strategies like influencer endorsements, algorithmic recommendations, and limited-time offers amplify these emotional responses, leading to impulsive and emotionally driven purchases. Using a combination of secondary research and survey-based data from adolescents aged 13-19, the paper finds that emotional satisfaction and peer influence are stronger motivators than practical necessity in digital spending. The research also highlights ethical concerns surrounding manipulative marketing tactics targeting young free consumers. Finally, it proposes integrating emotional and financial literacy education to help teenagers develop mindful consumption habits in an increasingly persuasive digital marketplace.

title: Performative Governance, Invisible Infrastructures and Operational Sovereignty. A MON × IIC Framework for Understanding State Capacity in Africa

detail.title: Performative Governance, Invisible Infrastructures and Operational Sovereignty. A MON × IIC Framework for Understanding State Capacity in Africa
detail.abstract:
African public policies produce laws, plans, and systems, yet without generating the expected productive transformation or decent jobs. This working paper proposes a conceptual framework explaining this persistent gap between visible reforms and real effects. By articulating the trilogy Metrology–Organization–Normativity (M–O–N) with the Invisible Infrastructures of Capital (IIC), it shows that the four structural impasses — weak domestic capital, massive dead capital, SMEs outside the productive paradigm, and structural informal employment — all stem from a single cause: the absence of institutional infrastructures capable of making capital visible, traceable, and operational.

The approach is abductive and comparative, illustrated through three cases (programme budgeting, SME finance, and digital administration). It demonstrates that MON deficits (weak indicators, fragmented coordination, limited appropriation) are only the symptoms of a deeper fragility of the IIC. The international comparison (Asia/Africa) confirms that divergence does not originate from initial GDP levels, but from the unequal depth of these infrastructures.

The core contribution is to propose performative governance as the missing link between state capability and productive transformation: economic sovereignty begins with operational sovereignty.

title: Vietnam Music Landscape 2025 - 2026: Glocalisation, Identity, Synergy
affiliations: Royal Melbourne Institute of Technology (RMIT University), RMIT University Vietnam, RMIT University Vietnam, RMIT University Vietnam and RMIT University Vietnam

detail.title: Vietnam Music Landscape 2025 - 2026: Glocalisation, Identity, Synergy
detail.abstract:
The year 2025 marks a remarkable transformation for Vietnam’s music market and cultural industry, reflecting not only growth in quantity but also a significant leap in quality. We have witnessed an unprecedented surge of large-scale events (tiers A50–A80) alongside a series of high-profile international performances, where Vietnamese audiences showcased their sophistication, enthusiasm, and class. At the same time, Vietnamese artists have consecutively achieved impressive milestones, asserting their position and increasingly broad influence. This vividly demonstrates that the cultural industry, with Vietnam’s music ecosystem at its core, is operating vibrantly with active participation from the government, businesses, brands, and fan communities.
However, behind this dazzling picture lie considerable challenges in elevating the music industry to a new level. To truly compete with regional and global music markets, the sector requires comprehensive professionalization, sustainable development strategies, and above all, the cultivation of a distinctive, unique V-Pop identity. The time has come not only to organize large-scale events but also to build a cultural industry with depth and character.
So how can the successes of 2025 be transformed into long-term growth momentum? What are the keys to establishing a distinctive V-Pop identity on the international stage? How are new standards of professionalism and sustainability defined in this evolving context? And which trends will lead the market in 2026? The Vietnam Music Landscape 2025–2026 whitepaper, continuously updated by the Research Team of the School of Communication and Design at RMIT University Vietnam, provides the public with a comprehensive picture of the standout achievements of 2025, while offering in-depth analysis of challenges and insights into strategic trends for the development of the industry in the coming period.

title: Multi-Stakeholder Marketing in Practice: Actionable Advice for Responsible Marketers
affiliations: and University of Turin - Department of Management

detail.title: Multi-Stakeholder Marketing in Practice: Actionable Advice for Responsible Marketers
detail.abstract: Purpose-This study bridges the gap between the theory and the practice of multi-stakeholder marketing (MSM) by accomplishing three main goals. First, it provides examples of how MSM is operationalized into the 7Ps of the marketing mix and offers actionable insights to marketing managers. Second, it outlines the practical drivers leading to MSM. Third, it identifies firms' clusters of MSM implementation stages. Design/methodology/approach-We collected data through semi-structured interviews in a podcast format, designed and conducted by the authors of this study. The interviews involved 45 managers and entrepreneurs operating in Italy from multinational companies (MNCs) and small and medium-sizedenterprises (SMEs) in various industries. Thematic and content analyses were applied. Findings-We discuss a new interpretation of the 7Ps of the marketing mix according to MSM, revealing that having a purpose-driven mindset, establishing an active dialogue with stakeholders, developing an innovationoriented leadership and enacting a cross-functional approach within organizations can lead to adequate MSM. Research limitations/implications-The study employs a qualitative analysis of 45 interviews conducted in Italy, with most firms operating in international markets, primarily with managers of MNCs and SMEs. While rich in insights, the sample limits generalizability to other contexts, opening the way for further crosscountry and sector-specific qualitative and quantitative studies. Practical implications-We provide actionable insights into MSM to marketing managers that derive from real-life examples and considerations developed around each of the 7Ps of the marketing mix, demonstrating how MSM can be incorporated into marketing strategies and tactics, from product development to promotion and pricing, showing successful cases from the Podcast. Originality/value-This study builds a bridge between theoretical conceptualizations of MSM and its practical implementation, which is timely and relevant not only theoretically but especially for marketing professionals. Using interviews from the podcast as a data source provides an innovative, narrative and sincere methodology that enriches the discourse on stakeholder-oriented and more responsible marketing practices.

title: Draft Innovation Ecosystem Lifecycle
affiliations: TUM School of Management,Technical University of Munich

detail.title: Draft Innovation Ecosystem Lifecycle
detail.abstract: Innovation ecosystems are dynamic socio-technical structures that evolve through identifiable patterns of emergence, growth, maturity, and renewal. Despite extensive conceptual development, the temporal dynamics underlying ecosystem evolution remain insufficiently understood and rarely measured. This paper develops and empirically validates a dynamic, indicator-based lifecycle model that operationalizes ecosystem evolution using longitudinal data on patents and venture capital. Drawing on six metropolitan regions, Munich, Boston, Zurich, Stockholm, Tel Aviv, and Austin, the model identifies temporal inflection points in innovation and entrepreneurial capacity as signatures of stage transitions. By translating lifecycle theory from a primarily descriptive analogy into a quantifiable analytical framework, the study provides the first empirical demonstration that ecosystem development follows recurrent and measurable trajectories. The findings show that structural expansion, entrepreneurial scaling, and governance adaptation unfold in patterned sequences, and that renewal capacity depends on the co-evolution of technological and entrepreneurial activity. Conceptually, the model advances research on innovation ecosystems by integrating structural, relational, and temporal dimensions within a single dynamic framework. For policy, it provides a stage-sensitive diagnostic tool that can inform targeted interventions and enhance the design of regional innovation strategies. The study thus reframes innovation ecosystems as adaptive and cyclical systems, contributing a replicable approach for analyzing their evolution across spatial and institutional contexts.

title: Inovasi E-commerce Sebagai Penggerak Kewirausahaan Modern Dalam Menjawab Tantangan Dan Kebutuhan Abad Ke-21

detail.title: Inovasi E-commerce Sebagai Penggerak Kewirausahaan Modern Dalam Menjawab Tantangan Dan Kebutuhan Abad Ke-21
detail.abstract: This paper aims to describe how e-commerce serves as a major driver of modern entrepreneurship in responding to various challenges and societal needs in the 21st century. Advances in digital technology have significantly transformed business patterns, requiring entrepreneurs to adapt to online-based marketing and transaction systems. The writing method used is a literature review through the examination of previous studies, digital industry development reports, and concepts related to technology-based entrepreneurship. The discussion focuses on the ability of e-commerce to provide new opportunities, such as wider market access, more efficient business processes, and innovative services. This article also presents an overview of an environmental engagement model that involves collaboration among entrepreneurs, consumers, digital service providers, and online communities to build an adaptive and sustainable entrepreneurial ecosystem. The findings indicate that e-commerce enhances business competitiveness while also opening opportunities for new entrepreneurs to grow without geographical limitations. In conclusion, e-commerce functions as a driver of innovation, an accelerator of economic growth, and a strategic solution to meet the demands of modern society, which prioritizes speed, convenience, and technology-based efficiency.

title: Exploring Managerial Challenges and Opportunities in Implementing Smart Pharmacies: A Qualitative Study Using Grounded Theory Approach in Iran
affiliations: Payame Noor University, Payam-e-Noor University and Payam-e-Noor University

detail.title: Exploring Managerial Challenges and Opportunities in Implementing Smart Pharmacies: A Qualitative Study Using Grounded Theory Approach in Iran
detail.abstract: Background: The implementation of smart pharmacies represents a significant advancement in healthcare technology, offering potential benefits in medication management and patient care. However, the transition to these systems presents unique challenges, particularly in developing countries like Iran. This study aims to investigate the managerial challenges and opportunities associated with implementing smart pharmacies in Iran using a grounded theory approach. Methods: This qualitative study employed a grounded theory approach. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 25 participants, including pharmacy managers, healthcare administrators, and IT specialists from various regions of Iran. Data were analyzed using constant comparative analysis and open, axial, and selective coding techniques. MAXQDA software (version 2020) was used for data management and analysis. Results: The analysis revealed five main categories: (1) technological infrastructure barriers, (2) regulatory and policy challenges, (3) human resource management issues, (4) financial constraints, and (5) opportunities for innovation and efficiency. A core category emerged: "Navigating the digital transformation of pharmacy services in a resource-constrained environment." The study identified key challenges such as inadequate IT infrastructure (reported by 80% of participants), resistance to change among staff (65%), and concerns about data security (72%). Opportunities included improved inventory management (reported by 85% of participants) and enhanced patient safety through reduced medication errors (78%). Conclusion: While smart pharmacies offer significant potential for improving pharmaceutical services in Iran, their implementation faces multifaceted challenges. Addressing these challenges requires a comprehensive approach involving stakeholder collaboration, targeted investment in infrastructure, and tailored training programs. The findings provide valuable insights for policymakers and healthcare managers in developing strategies for the successful integration of smart pharmacy systems in Iran and similar contexts.

title: Robot Money: Machine-Native Liquidity and Deterministic Economic Coordination

detail.abstract: Autonomous systems depend on continuous access to energy, compute, connectivity, and storage, and they must acquire these resources within fixed control cycles. When resource access requires a financial transfer, settlement becomes an operational requirement. This paper develops an economic framework that links deterministic settlement to the feasibility of autonomous operation. It defines robot money as liquidity that can be used within deterministic intervals, enabling autonomous systems to confirm resource availability, maintain solvency, and schedule tasks according to machine time. The analysis formalizes the machine balance sheet, the solvency condition, and the interval-bound optimization that structure task selection and liquidity allocation. These mechanisms generate market-level outcomes, including adaptive liquidity surfaces, cyber-physical arbitrage, and patterns of policy convergence. The paper identifies propagation, amplification, and congestion as key features of deterministic systemic dynamics. The framework concludes with a governance and supervisory model grounded in credentialed autonomy, functional safety principles, and PFMI standards.

detail.abstract: This paper develops an original theoretical framework-Guo's Starbucks Stability Hypothesis-arguing that the density of Starbucks coffee stores in a given polity serves as an interpretable indicator of political stability. The hypothesis diverges from classical globalization theories that assume economic interdependence alone constrains conflict. Whereas the "Golden Arches Theory" posited that states hosting McDonald's franchises would avoid war, contemporary events demonstrate that broad consumer capitalism does not automatically prevent violence. By contrast, Starbucks stores require a specific set of institutional conditions-middle class consumption, predictable regulation, infrastructure reliability and global supply chain integration. This paper synthesises insights from international political economy, urban sociology, and consumption studies to propose that Starbucks density captures micro level governance attributes neglected by macroeconomic indicators. Drawing on conflict data, urbanisation research and coffee-consumption scholarship, the paper outlines mechanisms linking Starbucks presence to stable political order. The result is a nuanced framework for analysing how everyday consumer infrastructures reflect deeper structures of stability and invites further empirical testing.

detail.abstract: Mauritius offers an instructive case of how a Small Island Developing State (SIDS) navigates the intersection of climate vulnerability, financial-sector sophistication and ESG transformation. Despite acute climate risks, the country hosts one of Africa’s most developed international financial centres and a capital market dominated by family-owned conglomerates. This paper examines the macroeconomic, regulatory, governance and ownership structures shaping Mauritius’ ESG transition, including demographic and fiscal trends, AML/CFT reforms following FATF grey-listing, and the emergence of sustainable finance instruments such as green and sustainability-linked bonds. It analyses how concentrated ownership, low free float and thin market liquidity affect ESG adoption, disclosure quality and capital-market responsiveness. The paper concludes that Mauritius stands at a critical juncture: a climate-exposed IFC with the potential to become a leading African laboratory for climate-smart capitalism, contingent on improved ESG data, stronger regulatory capacity and closer alignment between government, regulators and dominant corporate actors.

detail.abstract: This paper analyzes the growing scholarly consensus that the United States is experiencing significant democratic backsliding following Donald Trump’s return to the presidency in 2024. Drawing on established research in comparative political science, including frameworks of competitive authoritarianism, democratic erosion, and personalist parties, this paper examines how institutional norms and constraints are being weakened through targeted policies, civil service politicization, emergency power expansion, and attacks on independent institutions. Key mechanisms such as Schedule F, proposed uses of the Insurrection Act and Alien Enemies Act, and the transformation of the Republican Party into a leader-centric organization are evaluated in light of global patterns of authoritarian consolidation. Evidence from political science surveys, legal analyses, and expert commentary suggests that these developments resemble the trajectories seen in contemporary competitive authoritarian regimes such as Hungary and Turkey. The paper concludes that taken together, these actions pose substantial risks to the integrity of American democratic institutions and the maintenance of liberal democratic norms.

title: A Model of Religious Education from Birth to Age 3

detail.title: A Model of Religious Education from Birth to Age 3
detail.abstract: Introduction: Religious education is an activity aimed at shaping and transforming religious identity. A psychological analysis of the process of religious identity formation in the mental system reveals that from birth to eighteen years, four distinct models of religious identity emerge based on the child's cognitive development. From birth to three years, the initial roots of religious identity are formed. When language and thought emerge and converge between the ages of three to seven, the first model of religious identity in the child is shaped, reflecting the outward and visible aspects of adult faith. The third model of religious identity is formed between the ages of seven to twelve, imitating the system beliefs and values of the social context in which the child lives. During adolescence, the first reflections and revisions of the identity formed in the previous stage begin, and the first model of religious identity based on the adolescent's choice is shaped. Since the model of religious education at each age stage is based on the achievable and specific religious identity model of that stage, four models of religious education can be discussed from birth to eighteen years. Therefore, the purpose of the religious education model is to provide a roadmap for shaping and transforming religious identity, appropriate to its achievable level, for different life stages. This study aims to present a model of religious education from birth to three years, examining the five dimensions of the model based on a psychological analysis of the child's capacity to shape religious identity in this age range. The five dimensions of the model include 1) the achievable objectives of religious education; 2) the nature and source of religious education content from birth to three years; 3) methods for forming the initial foundations of faith; 4) the role of the educator and the cognitive, emotional, and skilled characteristics required to achieve the objectives; 5) methods for evaluating the attainment of the religious education objectives.

detail.abstract: Increasing weather-driven disruptions to water supplies have raised growing concerns about the resilience of drinking water infrastructure and equitable access to safe drinking water during severe weather events. This study seeks to address gaps in evaluating and understanding the resilience of community water systems (CWSs) to severe weather events at regional scales, including both the physical infrastructure and population served. We developed an approach that combines boil water notice (BWN) occurrence and duration as a metric of CWS performance and bottled water sales to capture community response to water disruptions. We conducted fixed-effects panel regressions to quantify relationships of these metrics to severe weather events and operational and sociodemographic characteristics using a statewide analysis of Texas, United States from 2010-2022. We found that small, publicly owned, and groundwater-sourced CWSs are most susceptible to BWNs. Hurricanes and winter weather significantly increased BWN duration by 2.0 and 0.68 days, respectively. During weather-driven BWNs, high-income communities had the greatest increase in bottled water purchasing (+58.3%) while low-income communities had a significantly lower increase (+5.6%). This study provides a better understanding of differences in vulnerability of CWSs to weather events and associated response of populations served at regional scales.

detail.abstract: Many experts see China’s economy as constrained because of a weak social safety net, especially the retirement system, resulting in anemic domestic consumption spending. This view is out of date. Recent data indicate that China has expanded many parts of its social safety net and that consumption spending has accelerated. Social expenditures in China have more than doubled as a share of GDP since 2010 and are on par with Mexico and Turkey. But given China’s aging population, safety net spending and domestic consumption spending will need to expand further to put China’s economy on a more sustainable path. The latest data should clear the cobwebs of misunderstanding that have led to both complacency and unnecessary alarm about China’s economic prospects among observers in the United States and other countries. China’s government is hardly unaware of the importance of stronger household consumption and has announced policies to increase consumer spending, including more generous pension benefits for farmers and rural migrant workers. If these initiatives are implemented, the growth of household consumption is likely to accelerate.

detail.abstract:
Contemporary civil law relies heavily on private ordering to determine the substantive content of social and economic relationships. Yet the institutional environment in which this private norm production occurs is fragmented, opaque, and structurally incapable of evolving at the pace demanded by modern life. Statutory law changes slowly, while powerful private actors fill the resulting vacuum through standard-form contracts that function as de facto legislation. This asymmetry concentrates rule-making authority in the hands of parties with disproportionate bargaining power and prevents society from collectively improving the normative architectures that govern everyday relationships.

This paper introduces Open-Source Civil Law (OSCL) as a protocol-based framework that reconciles the adaptability of private ordering with the stability of public law. OSCL reconceptualizes civil law as a multi-layered system consisting of a state-controlled kernel of mandatory rules, a collaboratively governed protocol layer of modular legal components, and an application layer of private agreements that import and extend these components. Drawing on principles from open-source software development, semantic versioning, and distributed governance, OSCL supplies the infrastructure for transparent, auditable, and collectively refined evolution of civil norms.

The framework does not replace state authority; it formalizes the interface between autonomy and public oversight, enabling legal systems to evolve with greater granularity and responsiveness. By transforming private-law rule-making from a fragmented and asymmetric practice into a collaborative, versioned, and openly governed process, OSCL democratizes the production of civil norms and offers a new model for institutional innovation. The result is a structural blueprint for an “institutional GitHub,” through which society can continuously refine the legal architectures that shape its relationships.

title: High Cost of Decarbonization in the Transport Industry

detail.title: High Cost of Decarbonization in the Transport Industry
detail.abstract: Decarbonizing the transport sector is a central pillar of modern climate policy, yet full electrification of heavy-duty commercial fleets remains financially and operationally prohibitive in the near term. Current analyses estimate that upgrading the U.S. commercial vehicle fleet with high-power charging infrastructure, substations, and grid enhancements will require investments in the hundreds of billions of dollars, with per-vehicle infrastructure costs reaching tens or even hundreds of thousands. These barriers—combined with long deployment timelines and operational limitations of electric and hydrogen technologies—create a significant risk of delayed climate benefits. This case study examines FuelWell, a plug-and-play catalytic system that enhances combustion efficiency in existing internal-combustion engines, reducing fuel consumption by 10–20% without requiring engine modifications or infrastructure updates. Field and laboratory data show annual savings of 6,000–12,000 USD and 20–40 tons of CO₂ per truck, with payback periods from several months to under one year. Scaled to fleets of thousands of vehicles, the technology offers immediate, low-CAPEX emissions reductions in the order of millions of tons of CO₂ annually, complementing long-term electrification strategies. Positioned as a transitional measure, FuelWell enables rapid environmental gains, mitigates cost and grid-capacity challenges, and provides a pragmatic pathway for accelerating national decarbonization while long-horizon infrastructure projects mature.

detail.abstract: Research shows that competition negatively impacts fund alpha. I derive that fund managers can counteract this impact by adjusting the level of active management. detail.abstract: The CHIPS and Science Act, enacted in August 2022, is a key element of the revival of U.S. industrial policy. We examine the short-term employment effects of the act. Drawing on quarterly industry-by-county data from the Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages (QCEW), we implement two county-level difference-in-difference designs, the first comparing counties with pre-existing semiconductor facilities to other counties with high-tech industries and the second comparing counties with semiconductor fabrication facilities (which were targeted for the bulk of the CHIPS funding) to counties with non-fabrication semiconductor facilities. Using both approaches, we find robust, positive employment impacts in affected counties. The effects began at the time of the passage in the Senate of a precursor bill, in anticipation of the signing of the CHIPS Act. Our preferred estimates suggest an increase of 110 jobs per affected county in the first design and 180 jobs per affected county in the second design. Simple back-of-the-envelope calculations suggest national direct employment effects of approximately 15,000-16,000 jobs in the core semiconductor sector and indirect effects of 28,000-35,000 jobs in related sectors.

title: Case Study: Orbital Improvisation Under Fire -The Shenzhou-20/21 Crew Swap and Its Ripple Effects on Tiangong Operations

detail.title: Case Study: Orbital Improvisation Under Fire -The Shenzhou-20/21 Crew Swap and Its Ripple Effects on Tiangong Operations
detail.abstract: Picture this: You're 400 kilometers above Earth, your ride home's got a hairline fracture from a speck of cosmic shrapnel, and the clock's ticking on your oxygen and sanity. That's the nail-biter China Manned Space Agency (CMSA) faced in November 2025 with the Shenzhou-20 mission. What started as a routine six-month stint on the Tiangong space station turned into the first-ever in-orbit crew vehicle swap due to space debris damage. Drawing on real-time CMSA releases, crew debriefs, and orbital telemetry analyses, this case unpacks the incident's anatomy-from the "tiny cracks" in the return capsule to today's successful docking of the emergency Shenzhou-22 lifeboat, prepared in a blistering 16-day crash program We spotlight the human ingenuity behind it: pre-baked redundancies, lightning-fast decision loops, and a handover "sprint" that kept science rolling amid chaos. Lessons? In megaprojects-from space stations to megadams-treat debris (literal or figurative) as a feature, not a bug. This isn't just aerospace arcana; it's a blueprint for any team staring down black swans. Implications for PM practitioners: Bake in modularity early, rehearse the unthinkable, and remember-resilience isn't about avoiding storms, it's dancing in them.

detail.abstract: This project presents the design, implementation, and validation of a custom-built, open-source, protocol focused on efficiency, reliability and simplicity. The protocol is designed to work within a client server architecture ensuring security, synchronization and scalability. The protocol operates over TCP (Transmission control protocol) leveraging its in-order delivery and retransmission guarantees to maintain synchronization without the need for custom reliability mechanisms. title: The Attention-Driven Phillips Curve: Rational Inattention, Policy Errors, and Microfounded Welfare

detail.title: The Attention-Driven Phillips Curve: Rational Inattention, Policy Errors, and Microfounded Welfare
detail.abstract: This paper demonstrates that ignoring firms' rational inattention to competing inflation drivers generates systematic policy errors and microfounded welfare losses. We develop a New Keynesian model where firms allocate limited attention across supply, financial, and structural inflation drivers, yielding a Phillips Curve with endogenously time-varying weights. We derive the social welfare function from household preferences and prove that using a fixed-weight Phillips Curve creates quadratic welfare losses during attention reallocations. Empirically, we estimate the model on 15 advanced economies (1990-2024) using the Global Financial Cycle for identification. The structural model outperforms benchmarks, particularly during attention shifts, and counterfactual analysis shows welfare losses of 15-30% during crises. Our results provide a rigorous justification for incorporating attention reallocation in monetary policy models.

detail.title: Delay-and-Pay: Prolonging Pharmaceutical Patent Protection Without Paying the “Price”
detail.abstract: This article argues that actors use the patent system as part of a “delay-and-pay” strategy to preserve drug prices for as long as possible by delaying generic/biosimilar market entry – and that they have a significant financial incentive to do so. This strategy is based on the notion that it is much more profitable for patentees to delay generic/biosimilar market entry by way of a patent infringement claim and ensuing injunction, then pay damages to the enjoined party should the infringement claim be defeated. Indeed, patentees have much to gain and little to lose under “delay-and-pay”. My analysis establishes that the money national health bodies  spent purchasing the more expensive, patented drug whilst the interim injunction remained in effect is not usually compensated following a patent revocation and discharged injunction. That is neither just, nor fair: the losses of national health bodies ought to be recovered.

title: The Islamic Governance and Secular State (Philosophical Tensions and Practical Possibilities)
affiliations: Superior University

detail.title: The Islamic Governance and Secular State (Philosophical Tensions and Practical Possibilities)
detail.abstract:
This article looks at how a modern secular state and an Islamic system of government interact. It focuses on the clashes that happen when God’s laws meet modern human reasoning, and also explores ways the two might work together.

Secularism is based on Enlightenment thinking; values human freedom, logical decision-making, and keeping the government neutral toward religion. Islamic governance, on the other hand, sees political power as a sacred duty (amanah) guided by God’s law (Shari‘ah – شریعت) and aimed at creating justice (‘adl – عدل) and public good (maslahah – مصلحہ).

Because of these differences, people continue to debate what makes a government truly legitimate, how religion should be part of public life, and what concepts like freedom and justice really mean.
This study looks at both classical Muslim thinkers; like al-Mawardi and Ibn Khaldun and modern reformers such as Fazlur Rahman and Abdullahi an-Na‘im. It argues that Islam and secularism don’t have to be in conflict. By examining countries like Turkey, Indonesia, Malaysia, and Tunisia, the study shows how mixed political systems have emerged ones that combine modern secular institutions with Islamic moral values. These examples prove that both approaches can work together when politics is built on shared ethics, mutual compromise, and an understanding of Shari‘ah’s broader goals (maqasid al-shari‘ah).

Ultimately, the paper proposes that secularism and Islamic governance should not be viewed as adversarial systems but as complementary moral frameworks that pursue justice and human dignity through distinct yet intersecting paths. For Muslim-majority societies, the real challenge lies not in choosing between religion and modernity, but in crafting political systems that uphold both spiritual integrity and civic liberty a goal attainable through sustained philosophical engagement, institutional innovation, and moral resolve.

detail.abstract: This paper consolidates multivariate variables to offer a new approach to estimating the costs of handloom products. Data consisting of preprocessed handloom goods’ pricing, size, fabric type, colour, and design features were collected. Due to the highly intensive work characteristic of the handloom industry and its perceived cultural value, the latter struggles to establish appropriate prices mainly because of design density, fabrics used and colour options available. Therefore, the accurate prediction of prices is the best way to ensure the fairness of trades and the sustainability of crafts people’s lives. Based on these important variables, this study develops a forecast model of handloom prices by employing the Decision Tree Regression model which is a machine-learning technique. The stakeholders in the handloom organized sector can use the model because it reflects complex interrelationships of price and features with high accuracy. This research also shows that the integration of several features enhances the price forecast, thereby enabling the handloom market decision-makers to make the right decisions.

title: The Long Run Economic Effects of Medical Innovation and the Role of Opportunities
affiliations: University of Warwick, University of Oxford - Department of Economics and University of Pennsylvania

detail.title: The Long Run Economic Effects of Medical Innovation and the Role of Opportunities

publicationDetails.journalName: NBER Working Paper Series

detail.abstract:
We leverage the introduction of the first antibiotic therapies in 1937 to examine the long-run effects of early-childhood pneumonia on adult educational attainment, employment, income, and work-related disability. Using census data, we document large average improvements across all outcomes, alongside substantial heterogeneity by gender and race. Among women, health gains led to changes in marriage and fertility that partially offset their labor market improvements. Among Black Americans, we uncover a pronounced gradient linked to systemic racial discrimination in the pre–Civil Rights era: individuals born in more discriminatory Jim Crow states realized much smaller gains than those born in less discriminatory states, despite larger reductions in pneumonia exposure. There is no similar gradient among white Americans. Together, these findings highlight the central role of institutional environments in shaping whether investments in early-life health translate into long-run socioeconomic gains.

detail.abstract: We study how artificial intelligence adoption reshapes incentive contracts, employment relationships, and firm values in a dynamic general-equilibrium model with search frictions. Firms contract with skilled workers under moral hazard and outside options are endogenously determined through competitive rematching in the labor market. AI can either complement workers by increasing labor productivity or substitute for labor by providing firms with an alternative production technology. When AI adoption is firm-specific, labor-market conditions remain unchanged and contracts respond primarily through stronger incentives and uniformly higher effort. When complementary AI adoption is sector-wide, AI raises both firms' and workers' market values, alters the efficiency of termination, increases effort all the more as the agent has performed well, and increases termination payments. The anticipation of productivity shocks alters incentives and both labor market and firm outcomes. In contrast to complementary AI, substitutive AI strengthens termination threats. title: The effects of interbank market on Central Bank Digital Currency and Transmission of Monetary Policy
affiliations: , National Research University Higher School of Economics (HSE) and Central University of Finance and Economics (CUFE)

detail.title: The effects of interbank market on Central Bank Digital Currency and Transmission of Monetary Policy
detail.abstract: In this paper, we examine the transitional dynamics of central bank digital currency (CBDC) in an economy with heterogeneous banks and an interbank market, using a New Keynesian DSGE framework. Our findings show that the interbank market amplifies monetary policy shocks compared to a baseline scenario where the interbank market is absent or non-functional. Within the interbank setting, whether CBDC acts as a substitute for, or a complement to, bank deposits play a crucial role in either dampening or amplifying the transmission of monetary policy shocks. Furthermore, we find that the choice of policy instrument is critical in shaping outcomes in the presence of an interbank market.

title: Beyond the Barrel- A Dance of Profit and Purpose
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Beyond the Barrel- A Dance of Profit and Purpose
detail.abstract: Petroleum taxation in Nigeria is a balancing exercise that attempts to simultaneously satisfy the State's right to extract maximum value from its natural resources and the investor's need for fiscal certainty and capital recovery. This objective is pursued through an evolving legislative framework, moving from the Petroleum Profit Tax Act (PPT) to the Petroleum Industry Act (PIA) 2021, and most recently the Nigeria Tax Act (NTA) 2025. Historical frameworks suffered from administrative complexity and overlapping regimes, hindering predictable cost recovery. This paper investigates whether the consolidation of petroleum fiscal logic into the NTA strengthens revenue certainty while preserving investor rights. Using a legislative and comparative analysis, the study reviews the Tax Reform Acts, specifically examining cost recovery mechanisms and gas incentives. Findings reveal that the NTA reduces administrative discretion by centralizing authority under the Nigeria Revenue Service. The 65% Cost Price Ratio (CPR) acts as a fiscal anchor, ensuring the State receives revenue "from the first barrel" by capping deductible costs. Furthermore, the system enforces compliance through US dollar-denominated payments and escalating penalties. In contrast to the field-level flexibility of the UK and Norway, Nigeria employs "Behavioural Engineering" via rigid ceilings. Ultimately, while the framework enhances stability, it limits project-specific flexibility, forcing a choice of predictability over negotiated relief.

title: The SRDB Framework for Inflation Forecasting: A Regime-Sensitive, Principled Approach with External Validation
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: The SRDB Framework for Inflation Forecasting: A Regime-Sensitive, Principled Approach with External Validation
detail.abstract: This paper develops and validates an inflation forecasting framework grounded in the Systemic Risk of Doing Business (SRDB) principle. The central SRDB insight-that inflation reflects compensation for economy-wide risk generated by price adjustment frictions, financial intermediation constraints, and structural fragility-provides a unifying logic for organizing inflation dynamics across regimes. We translate this principle into a transparent, reduced-form Bayesian model that factorizes inflation into computational, financial, and structural risk channels with time-varying weights. The model demonstrates robust out-of-sample performance across eight advanced economies (1970-2024), achieving a 23.5 percent RMSE reduction against the standard BVAR benchmark. Crucially, it provides early warning of inflationary turning points with a 2.3quarter lead time, and its signals are externally validated by their ability to predict revisions in market inflation expectations and shifts in central bank communication. The SRDB framework offers a principled, coherent alternative to purely statistical or single-channel models for policymakers navigating structural transitions.

publicationDetails.detailsText: East Asian Economic Review Vol. 29, No. 4 (December 2025) pp. 415-453, https://dx.doi.org/10.11644/KIEP.EAER.2025.29.4.455

detail.abstract: In the context of rising geopolitical tensions and complex regulatory environments, Chinese pharmaceutical export enterprises face growing institutional barriers that hinder their participation in Global Value Chains (GVCs). Drawing on dynamic capability theory and contingency theory, this study examines how enterprise resiliencecomprising anticipatory and adaptive capabilities-facilitates international collaboration under institutional pressure. Using survey data from 319 managerial respondents of Chinese pharmaceutical export enterprises and hierarchical regression analysis, the results show that both anticipatory and adaptive capabilities are positively associated with GVC participation and restructuring. Additionally, the empirical evidence partially supports the proposed moderating effects of institutional barriers-namely institutional distance, institutional uncertainty, and institutional stringency. While these barriers do not significantly affect the relationship between resilience and GVC participation, they selectively weaken its positive relationship with GVC restructuring. These findings suggest the conditional role of enterprise resilience in navigating complex institutional environments and offer preliminary insights for policymakers to improve institutional conditions and mitigate the constraining effects of institutional barriers.

title: Second Chance: Life with Less Student Debt
affiliations: Imperial College Business School, Indiana University - Kelley School of Business - Department of Finance and Georgia State University - J. Mack Robinson College of Business

detail.title: Second Chance: Life with Less Student Debt
detail.abstract: We exploit an episode of plausibly random debt discharge due to the loss of paperwork for thousands of borrowers to examine the effects of private student debt relief on borrower outcomes. We find that borrowers who receive debt relief (treated) experience declines in debt balances and delinquency rates on other accounts, and increases in mobility and income relative to those who bear the costs of default like wage garnishment and collections (control). Borrowers in both groups contribute to our findings through different mechanisms. Although we cannot quantify its costs, our results speak to the benefits of loan forgiveness in reducing the consequences of debt burden for defaulted borrowers.

title: Decision Friction: Why Evidence-Rich Health Systems Still Fail to Decide

detail.title: Decision Friction: Why Evidence-Rich Health Systems Still Fail to Decide
detail.abstract: Health systems today operate in an environment of unprecedented evidence abundance. Advances in biomedical research, health economics, and data analytics have expanded what can be known about interventions, risks, and outcomes. Yet many evidence-rich health systems continue to exhibit delayed action, repeated reassessment, and persistent failure to translate knowledge into timely decisions. Prevailing explanations such as data gaps, uncertainty, political interference, or cognitive bias, do not adequately explain why decision paralysis persists where evidence is strong, expertise is high, and incentives are broadly aligned. This paper advances a system-level explanation for this paradox. It introduces Decision Friction as a novel theoretical construct describing the cumulative degradation of decision quality as evidence, authority, and accountability move through fragmented institutional decision architectures. In complex health systems, decisions are rarely discrete moments of choice; they are constructed through multi-stage processes of evaluation, negotiation, authorization, and operational translation across multiple actors and organizations. As decisions progress through these pathways, ownership becomes diffused, risk is displaced, and delays compound, often without any single point of failure or irrational behavior. To clarify mechanism, the paper develops the Decision Friction Funnel, identifying four recurring processes: signal dilution, erosion of ownership, risk displacement, and delay amplification. A central implication is counterintuitive: under certain institutional conditions, producing additional evidence can intensify Decision Friction rather than resolve it. The paper reframes decision failure as an architectural problem and outlines non-prescriptive principles for designing lower-friction decision pathways. Although developed in health systems, Decision Friction is proposed as a general property of complex governance systems.

title: Port Blockade and Export Shutdown
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Port Blockade and Export Shutdown
detail.abstract:
Ukraine was one of the global leaders in agricultural production even before the full-scale invasion in 2022. According to the European Commission, the country was among the top three global exporters of barley, corn, sunflower oil, and sunflower meal, as well as the fourth largest supplier of wheat. Access to deep-water ports on the Black Sea allowed 90% of Ukrainian agricultural goods to be transported by sea, providing billions in foreign exchange earnings and vital food security for many countries. In peacetime, grain logistics relied on an efficient system of ports, railways, and road transport. Before the war, about 75-80% of grain was exported through the deep-water ports of Odesa, Pivdennyi, and Chornomorsk, with the rest going via the Danube and smaller ports, while domestic transportation was fully provided by railcars and special road trains. The so-called balance between modes of transport kept logistics costs at an optimal level and allowed for a rapid response to changes in demand on world markets [1].

After the full-scale invasion and blockade of Ukrainian ports, this model was destroyed. Instead of the usual sea supply routes, it was necessary to find land corridors, build new partnerships, invest in technology, and implement digital tools for tracking cargo. At the same time, Ukraine and international organizations sought global solutions to prevent the global food crisis from escalating. In this case study, we will take a detailed and clear look at the preconditions for the blockade, its impact on the global market, international measures to restore exports, and the anti-crisis actions of Agro Region, which was able to maintain exports and avoid losses of more than $10-15 million by reorienting its logistics and innovatively restructuring its logistics department.

detail.abstract: We study equity valuation when investors benchmark firms against headline inflation although pass-through varies across firms. In standard valuation, inflation is valueneutral even with heterogeneous pass-through if investors use firm-specific inflation. Benchmarking to headline inflation conflates nominal cash-flow growth with real performance and shifts discount rates at inflation announcements. Pricing power shapes both channels by enabling greater pass-through and reducing perceived inflation exposure. Empirically, higher-pricing-power firms exhibit smaller stock-price declines and smaller cost-of-capital increases following inflation surprises. The April 2025 tariff announcement yields similar pricing-power-based return differences. These results offer new insights into inflation's implications for asset pricing and valuation.

detail.abstract: This study examines how digitalization influences income inequality in OECD countries, emphasizing that its effects depend on the stage of ICT development. Using panel data and a fixed-effects framework, we analyze four indicators of digitalization-fixed telephone subscriptions, mobile cellular subscriptions, individuals using the internet, and fixed broadband subscriptions-and interact them with a dummy capturing the transition to an advanced ICT era. The results show a clear stage-dependent pattern. In the early ICT-development period, digitalization reduces inequality by increasing income shares of the bottom four quintiles and reducing that of the top quintile. However, in the advanced ICT period, these equalizing effects weaken or reverse: digitalization becomes inequality-increasing, particularly for internet use and broadband subscriptions. The findings indicate that digitalization is not uniformly inclusive and underscore the need for policies that strengthen digital skills, broadband quality, and equitable participation in advanced digital ecosystems.

title: Lack Of Clear Structure in the Logistics Department
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Lack Of Clear Structure in the Logistics Department
detail.abstract: In today's agri-food sector, logistics is not limited to product delivery. It encompasses procurement planning, inventory management, transportation organization, supplier interaction, and document flow control. The logistics function is the “nervous system” of an enterprise, integrating production, finance, and marketing. Ukrainian studies have emphasized that the evolution of logistics organizational structures has gone through four stages: fragmentation (when logistics functions are scattered across different departments), functional aggregation (specialized logistics departments are formed), process integration (coordination of material, information, and financial flows), and networked integrated systems. In Ukraine, many companies still remain in the first two stages: logistics tasks are distributed across departments, which leads to conflicts, duplication of functions, and inflated costs [1]. The agro-industrial company Agro Region had a developed system for growing and selling grain, but its logistics operations were scattered. Different people were responsible for each area, namely purchasing, warehousing, and transportation. The lack of a single coordinator and KPIs led to errors in documentation, delivery delays, opaque costs, and a loss of trust among contractors. After the blockade of Ukrainian ports and the crisis, it became clear that without centralization and systematic evaluation of logistics processes, the company would not be able to remain competitive.

title: The Role of Social and Cultural Environments in Improving the Effectiveness of Student Entrepreneurship Activities in Samata, Gowa Regency

detail.title: The Role of Social and Cultural Environments in Improving the Effectiveness of Student Entrepreneurship Activities in Samata, Gowa Regency
detail.abstract: This study explores the role of the social and cultural environment in enhancing the effectiveness of student entrepreneurship activities in Samata, Gowa Regency. Using a qualitative approach with a descriptive-analytical design, this study involved participatory observation, in-depth interviews, and documentation analysis to identify the mechanisms of environmental involvement in the student entrepreneurship ecosystem. The results reveal that the social environment consists of five main components, including family networks, academic communities, student organizations, local businesses, and supporting institutions that interact to form a comprehensive support system. The cultural dimension, rooted in the values of siri' na pacce and sipakatau, sipakalebbi, sipakainge, shapes a work ethic and business orientation that considers social impact and collective responsibility. The environmental engagement model was identified through four mechanisms, namely family support, academic community empowerment, collaboration with local business actors, and the use of digital platforms. Effectiveness analysis shows that businesses with high environmental engagement have a sustainability rate of 83% with an average revenue growth of 32% per year. Supporting factors include geographical accessibility, digital infrastructure, and accommodative institutional policies, while inhibiting factors include socio-cultural expectation gaps, limited access to formal capital, and fragmentation of the entrepreneurial community. The research findings provide practical implications for the development of an inclusive and sustainable entrepreneurial ecosystem in higher education.

detail.abstract:
This paper advances Jurisdictional Signal Integrity (JSI) as a constitutional diagnostic framework for understanding modern representative strain in the absence of constitutional violation. It argues that contemporary dysfunction within Congress and related institutions cannot be adequately explained by partisanship, polarization, or institutional misconduct alone. Instead, the paper identifies a structural condition—Representational Signal Misalignment (RSM)—in which the communicative signal environment surrounding representative institutions exceeds or bypasses the jurisdictional and deliberative architecture through which those institutions are constitutionally designed to operate.

RSM is introduced as a novel descriptive concept rather than a theory of liability, reform agenda, or regulatory proposal. It names a condition in which lawful speech, protected participation, and formal procedural compliance coexist with measurable degradation in deliberative capacity, accountability clarity, institutional endurance, and representative retention. Under conditions of RSM, translation gives way to performance, authority decouples from audience standing, and rational actors adapt through exit or architectural migration—even in the absence of bad faith, ideological extremism, or electoral defeat.

Drawing on constitutional structure, institutional economics, and systems analysis, the paper traces the emergence of RSM to a late-twentieth-century broadcast inflection (circa 1979–1981), when national visibility and continuous media exposure altered the incentive environment of legislative service without corresponding changes to constitutional design. Empirical patterns—including elevated congressional attrition, declining legislative throughput, and migration toward executive offices—are examined as systems-level signals rather than episodic political anomalies.

The paper further explains why existing constitutional doctrines—separation of powers, federalism, First Amendment jurisprudence, and election law—are ill-suited to identify or remediate RSM. Courts increasingly sense democratic instability yet lack vocabulary to distinguish architectural degradation from political disagreement. JSI supplies that vocabulary while respecting justiciability boundaries, enabling recognition without prescribing judicial intervention.

Importantly, the paper does not advocate speech restriction, institutional redesign, or enforcement mechanisms. It treats constitutional stability as dependent not only on lawful authority and protected expression, but on preserved coherence between signal scope and institutional role. By recovering foundational disciplines—jurisdictional fidelity, deliberative restraint, and bounded accountability—JSI reframes constitutional harm as a condition that may arise without breach, and constitutional fidelity as a practice that may require restraint rather than assertion.

In doing so, the paper offers a pre-crisis interpretive framework for courts, legislators, and scholars confronting lawful governance under transformed communicative conditions, and situates Representational Signal Misalignment as a durable analytic concept for understanding constitutional erosion without constitutional failure.

detail.abstract: High cost of transport and logistics Introduction Until 2022, Ukraine's agricultural sector accounted for almost all of the country's export potential. The main route for grain delivery was by road from the fields to elevators and then by rail to the ports of Odesa, Chornomorsk, Pivdennyi, or Mykolaiv. The large-scale invasion and blockade of ports led to a significant restructuring of logistics. Farmers found themselves in a situation where delivering grain to port, with all the associated operating costs such as certification, loading, storage, and paperwork, cost twice as much as in European Union countries and 1.5 times more than in the United States [1]. As a result, logistics became the dominant cost component in the entire supply chain. This case study examines the problem of high transportation and logistics costs and the actions of the Agro Region team led by Khristina Gulida (initiator and project implementation manager), which made it possible to optimize costs and reduce them by 15-20%, as well as increase the predictability of logistics.
